fact: INEC Director of Elections Ramadhani Kailima said the voter register is by law made public during every stage of its update, and that it was provided to 18 political parties on 27 July 2025.
INEC says its Biometric Voter Registration kits, in use since 2019/2020, are being upgraded to an Android model for the March 2025 register update, with 3,427,917 voters registered in Dar es Salaam.
INEC says the new BVR kit has been upgraded to integrate with the NIDA database, and matches fingerprints against existing records to detect double registration.
INEC said it would update the Permanent Voters' Register from 1 July 2024 using upgraded Biometric Voter Registration kits, with the register projected at 34,746,638 voters after the update.

INEC chairperson Jacobs Mwambegele said the Preliminary Voters' Register would be publicly displayed during the second update of the Permanent Voter Register from 1 May 2025, so citizens could verify, correct or object to entries.
INEC says it secured 6,000 biometric voter registration kits to update the Permanent National Voters' Register for the 2025 elections, with an upgrade starting 20 July 2024.
INEC says online corrections to the voters register require a NIDA National Identification Number, which verifies the voter information being corrected.
INEC said in March 2025 it runs a Biometric Voter Registration Kit, now Android-based, feeding the Permanent Voter Register.

INEC's head of ICT said in March 2025 that voter registration is integrated with the NIDA database, so a voter's details are retrieved from NIDA by ID number; INEC on 23 August 2025 denied any integration with other systems for electoral purposes.
